_comment: VERIFIED-DATA-ONLY transfer trackers for La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga and Ligue 1 (2026/27). NOTHING is listed until it is officially confirmed by a club or widely reported by credible outlets — the PL tracker works this way and so do these. Club lists are shells based on the most recent completed season; the 2026/27 composition (promoted/relegated clubs) must be verified before publishing transfers. Paste verified entries into playersIn/playersOut with {player, from/to, type (Confirmed/Loan/Free/Released/Retired/Departed), detail}, manager name + note, rumours (never in confirmed tables), and notes.

clubs.name: Real Madrid
clubs.managerNote: New — second spell, replaced Xabi Alonso mid-season
clubs.notes: Mourinho's second spell begins with a statement window: Diomande for €125m and Cucurella for €55m headline the incomings, while Konaté and Bernardo Silva arrive on frees.

clubs.name: Barcelona
clubs.managerNote: No change
clubs.notes: Gordon's €80m arrival is the marquee deal, while Lewandowski departs on a free to MLS and Araújo heads to Liverpool on loan.

clubs.name: Atlético Madrid
clubs.managerNote: No change — 15th season in charge
clubs.notes: Simeone's 15th season brings a new creative core: Lee Kang-in and Hjulmand join for €40m each, while Griezmann's era ends with a free move to Orlando City.

clubs.name: Villarreal
clubs.managerNote: New — replaced Marcelino García Toral, who left after a contract dispute; Pérez guided Rayo Vallecano to last season's Conference League final
clubs.notes: Pérez arrives from Rayo after a Conference League final run, with Gulácsi adding experience in goal.

clubs.name: Athletic Club
clubs.managerNote: New
clubs.notes: Terzić takes over with no confirmed arrivals yet — departures so far are modest, with Vesga leaving on a free.

clubs.name: Real Betis
clubs.managerNote: No change
clubs.notes: Pellegrini rebuilds with Bernal and Fran García, with Altimira's €18.3m exit the biggest outgoing.

clubs.name: Real Sociedad
clubs.managerNote: New
clubs.notes: Matarazzo's first window is quiet so far, with Méndez's move to MLS the headline departure.

clubs.name: Sevilla
clubs.managerNote: New — arrived from Alavés
clubs.notes: Luis García Plaza brings Guridi with him from Alavés, while Azpilicueta retires after a storied career.

clubs.name: Valencia
clubs.managerNote: No change — in charge since 2024
clubs.notes: Corberán continues the rebuild with two low-cost additions in Sato and Deng.

clubs.name: Getafe
clubs.managerNote: No change — in charge since 2023
clubs.notes: Bordalás adds Satriano and Romero while two key midfielders depart.

clubs.name: Osasuna
clubs.managerNote: New — arrived from Espanyol
clubs.notes: Muñoz's €40m move to Liverpool is the club-record sale that funds Ramis' rebuild.

clubs.name: Rayo Vallecano
clubs.managerNote: New — arrived from SD Eibar, replaced Íñigo Pérez who left for Villarreal
clubs.notes: San José replaces Pérez, and club icon Óscar Trejo retires.

clubs.name: Celta Vigo
clubs.managerNote: No change — in charge since 2024
clubs.notes: Three free/low-cost additions strengthen Celta, with Bayindir arriving on loan from United.

clubs.name: Espanyol
clubs.managerNote: No change — in charge since 2024
clubs.notes: Moscardo's loan from PSG is the eye-catching move, with Calatrava arriving permanently.

clubs.name: Elche
clubs.managerNote: No change — in charge since 2024
clubs.notes: Rodríguez's €25m sale to Bournemouth funds a trio of additions including Buonanotte on loan.

clubs.name: Levante
clubs.managerNote: No change — in charge since 2025
clubs.notes: Espí's €25m move to Real Madrid is a club-record sale for Levante.

clubs.name: Alavés
clubs.managerNote: New — arrived from Sevilla
clubs.notes: Sánchez Flores returns after his Sevilla spell, with two additions and Guridi's free exit.

clubs.name: Deportivo de La Coruña
clubs.managerNote: No change — led the promotion campaign, arrived 2025 from SD Huesca
clubs.notes: Promoted Depor mean business: Aubameyang arrives for €1.5m to lead the line after promotion.

clubs.name: Real Racing Club
clubs.managerNote: No change — in charge since 2022, led the promotion
clubs.notes: Canales returning to Spanish football on a free is the standout signing for the promoted side.

clubs.name: Málaga
clubs.managerNote: No change — in charge since 2025, led the promotion
clubs.notes: Málaga's return to the top flight is marked by Calero arriving on a free and Luismi retiring.

leagues.name: Serie A
leagues.leagueNote: Nine clubs changed head coach this summer: Napoli, Milan, Atalanta, Bologna, Fiorentina, Lazio, Sassuolo, Torino and Monza.

clubs.name: Napoli
clubs.managerNote: New — replaced Antonio Conte, who left after two title-challenging seasons; contract to June 2029
rumours: Alexis Saelemaekers (Milan) — linked
Gabriel Jesus (Manchester United) — linked, low probability
Romelu Lukaku — Napoli have rejected a Fenerbahçe bid to keep him
clubs.notes: No major permanent signings confirmed yet — Allegri was only appointed on 3 June, so business is expected to accelerate.

clubs.name: Inter Milan
clubs.managerNote: No change — contract extended to 2028 after winning the title

playersOut.detail: Free transfer — replacement still being sought

clubs.notes: Title-winning Chivu adds Stones on a free and Spence from Spurs, but still needs to replace Dumfries.

clubs.name: AC Milan
clubs.managerNote: New — three-year deal to 2029
clubs.notes: Amorim's arrival is marked by the ~€74m signing of Gonçalo Ramos. Luka Modrić has extended his contract by one year — a renewal, not a transfer.

clubs.name: Juventus
clubs.managerNote: No change — contract to 2028
rumours: Dušan Vlahović — contract talks stalled; Chelsea linked
clubs.notes: Kolo Muani's loan becomes permanent, and Ekahtor arrives from Genoa for €16m.

clubs.name: Roma
clubs.managerNote: No change — leads Roma into the Champions League after a 3rd-place finish
rumours: Antonio Nusa (RB Leipzig) — linked
Mason Greenwood (Marseille) — linked
Rodrigo Mora (Porto) — linked
clubs.notes: Castro arrives from Bologna for ~€35m with Dovbyk heading the other way as part of the deal.

clubs.name: Atalanta
clubs.managerNote: New — reunites with sporting director Cristiano Giuntoli, three-year deal
rumours: Daniel Maldini — loan to Cagliari linked
El Bilal Touré — loan to Parma linked
Giorgio Scalvini — Newcastle interest reported
clubs.notes: Sarri takes over from Gasperini, whose era ended with a third-place finish.

clubs.name: Bologna
clubs.managerNote: New — returns to club football after the Belgium national team role
clubs.notes: Tedesco's return to club football sees Castro leave for Roma with Dovbyk arriving in the swap. Tommaso Pobega also arrived from Milan (€7m).

clubs.name: Fiorentina
clubs.managerNote: New
clubs.notes: Grosso's first window includes two Real Madrid additions. The club has stated Moise Kean is not for sale this window.

clubs.name: Como
clubs.managerNote: No change — first Champions League qualification in club history
clubs.notes: Champions League football brings statement signings: Chalobah and Morata both arrive.

clubs.name: Genoa
clubs.managerNote: No change
clubs.notes: Colombo returns permanently from Milan as Ekahtor departs for Juventus.

clubs.name: Lazio
clubs.managerNote: New — replaced Maurizio Sarri, three-year deal
rumours: Alessio Romagnoli — departure "seems inevitable" amid a reported relationship breakdown
Fabio Miretti — enquiry made to Juventus
clubs.notes: Gattuso replaces Sarri, with Gila's €30m exit to Milan the headline outgoing.

clubs.name: Sassuolo
clubs.managerNote: New
clubs.notes: Aquilani's first window has one confirmed departure so far.

clubs.name: Torino
clubs.managerNote: New
rumours: Alieu Njie and Gvidas Gineitis — both drawing interest from RB Salzburg (~£20m for the pair)
clubs.notes: Abate takes over with the club monitoring interest in two of its young stars.

clubs.name: Udinese
clubs.managerNote: No change
clubs.notes: No major confirmed transfers found yet for this snapshot.

clubs.name: Cagliari
clubs.managerNote: No change
rumours: Daniel Maldini — loan from Atalanta linked
clubs.notes: No major confirmed transfers found yet for this snapshot.

clubs.name: Lecce
clubs.managerNote: No change — contract auto-renewed to 2027 after securing survival, then extended to 2028
clubs.notes: No major confirmed transfers found yet for this snapshot.

clubs.name: Parma
clubs.managerNote: No change
rumours: El Bilal Touré — loan from Atalanta linked
David Romero (Tigre) — linked
clubs.notes: No major confirmed transfers found yet for this snapshot.

clubs.name: Venezia
clubs.managerNote: No change — led the promotion campaign
clubs.notes: Promoted Venezia make Akor Adams their club-record signing at €16m.

clubs.name: Monza
clubs.managerNote: New
clubs.notes: No major confirmed transfers found yet for this snapshot.

clubs.name: Frosinone
clubs.managerNote: New — led the promotion campaign; second Serie A stint after Cremonese in 2022/23
clubs.notes: No major confirmed transfers found yet for this snapshot.

leagues.name: Bundesliga
sources: Wikipedia (List of German football transfers summer 2026)

clubs.name: Bayern Munich
clubs.managerNote: No change — contract to 2029; last season set the Bundesliga record for goals scored in a campaign (122) and won the domestic double
clubs.notes: Kompany's champions add Saibari and Brown for a combined ~€105m. Manuel Neuer has signed a one-year contract extension — a renewal, not a transfer.

clubs.name: Borussia Dortmund
clubs.managerNote: No change — led BVB to 2nd place in 2025/26 with the league's best defence
rumours: Felix Nmecha — drawing interest from Manchester United and Chelsea
clubs.notes: Karetsas, 18, arrives from Genk as the headline signing after a strong 2025/26.

clubs.name: RB Leipzig
clubs.managerNote: New — replaced Ole Werner despite Leipzig finishing 3rd
clubs.notes: Demichelis takes over from Werner despite a 3rd-place finish, with Estève the marquee arrival.

clubs.name: Bayer Leverkusen
clubs.managerNote: New — Leverkusen's third head coach in a year, after Erik ten Hag and Kasper Hjulmand; arrives from Toulouse

playersIn.detail: 24-year-old joins as part of the squad rebuild (per betinf)

rumours: AC Milan have made a move to sign a Leverkusen player
clubs.notes: Leverkusen's third coach in a year begins a squad rebuild with a 24-year-old arrival from Napoli.

clubs.name: VfB Stuttgart
clubs.managerNote: No change — has taken Stuttgart to two DFB Cup finals and two Champions League qualifications
clubs.notes: Sauer's move from Feyenoord headlines a tidy window under Hoeneß.

clubs.name: Eintracht Frankfurt
clubs.managerNote: New — returning for a second spell, replacing Albert Riera
clubs.notes: Hütter's return is financed by Brown's ~€50m sale to Bayern, with Nkili arriving from the same club.

clubs.name: TSG Hoffenheim
clubs.managerNote: No change — signed a new long-term contract in May after a 5th-place finish and Europa League qualification
clubs.notes: Ilzer's Europa League side loses Prömel plus out-of-contract Akpoguma and Bebou.

clubs.name: SC Freiburg
clubs.managerNote: No change — led Freiburg to their first-ever European final, the Europa League, losing to Aston Villa
clubs.notes: Etringer graduates from the U19s and is immediately loaned to Elversberg, while veteran Höfler retires.

clubs.name: FC Augsburg
clubs.managerNote: No change — earned a further two-year contract after almost qualifying for Europe
clubs.notes: A quiet window so far, with Behrens returning from loan.

clubs.name: Mainz 05
clubs.managerNote: No change — took Mainz from relegation trouble to mid-table safety and a Conference League quarter-final in his first half-season
clubs.notes: No major confirmed transfers found yet for this snapshot.

clubs.name: Union Berlin
clubs.managerNote: New — arrives after winning the Swiss Super League with Thun
clubs.notes: Nsoki's loan is made permanent as Lustrinelli begins his first window.

clubs.name: Borussia Mönchengladbach
clubs.managerNote: No change — took over on an interim basis in November 2025, now permanent after a 12th-place finish
clubs.notes: No major confirmed transfers found yet for this snapshot.

clubs.name: Hamburger SV
clubs.managerNote: No change — led HSV to promotion in 2024/25 and a 13th-place finish on return to the top flight
clubs.notes: HSV secure Poręba permanently after his loan.

clubs.name: 1. FC Köln
clubs.managerNote: No change — took over as interim in March 2026 after Lukas Kwasniok, then earned a permanent two-year deal
clubs.notes: Baack is the only confirmed arrival so far.

clubs.name: Werder Bremen
clubs.managerNote: No change — steered Bremen away from the relegation zone after taking over in February 2026; first Bundesliga job
clubs.notes: Backhaus arrives as Thioune's first full-summer signing.

clubs.name: FC Schalke 04
clubs.managerNote: No change — won the 2. Bundesliga title to end Schalke's three-year top-flight absence
clubs.notes: Promoted Schalke bring in Adamu as they return to the top flight.

clubs.name: SV Elversberg
clubs.managerNote: No change — guided Elversberg to their first-ever Bundesliga promotion as runners-up
clubs.notes: Etringer arrives on loan from Freiburg for their historic top-flight debut.

clubs.name: SC Paderborn
clubs.managerNote: No change — beat Wolfsburg in the promotion play-off, 2–1 on aggregate
clubs.notes: Play-off winners Paderborn add Đurić and Noll from Hoffenheim.

leagues.name: Ligue 1
leagues.leagueNote: 18 clubs, 12 with a new head coach this summer — a record for Ligue 1, beating the previous high of 9 (matched in 2002/03, 2009/10 and 2021/22). Metz and Nantes were relegated to Ligue 2; Troyes and Le Mans came up in their place. The transfer window opened 15 June 2026.

clubs.name: Paris Saint-Germain
clubs.managerNote: No change — one of only six Ligue 1 clubs keeping its coach this summer

playersIn.detail: Permanent, undisclosed fee — after a loan spell last season

clubs.notes: PSG retained the European Super Cup on penalties against Aston Villa this week, while Ramos (~€74m) and Lee Kang-in (~€40m) depart.

clubs.name: Olympique de Marseille
clubs.managerNote: New — replaced Habib Beye; Génésio departed Lille for this role
clubs.notes: Génésio's Marseille rebuild brings five permanent arrivals and four high-profile loans, with Greenwood and Aubameyang departing.

clubs.name: AS Monaco
clubs.managerNote: New — replaced Sébastien Pocognoli
rumours: Troyes forward Mathys Detourbet — sold to Manchester City, expected to be loaned to Monaco this window
clubs.notes: Filipe Luís' first window is funded by Bamba's ~€35.5m sale to Newcastle, with Abline arriving for ~€25m.

clubs.name: Olympique Lyonnais
clubs.managerNote: No change — in charge since January 2025

playersIn.detail: Fee not disclosed — per Barcelona's tracker this is a separate Adeyemi deal to confirm; treat with caution, recheck

clubs.notes: Lyon's Adeyemi arrival is flagged for rechecking — the source itself advises caution on this item.

clubs.name: Lille (LOSC)
clubs.managerNote: New — son of Carlo Ancelotti, previously Botafogo and long-time Real Madrid/Bayern/Napoli/Brazil assistant; replaced Bruno Génésio, who left for Marseille; two-year deal
clubs.notes: No major permanent signings confirmed yet for this snapshot — recheck as the window nears its close.

clubs.name: OGC Nice
clubs.managerNote: New — arrived from Lorient, replacing Claude Puel after a season that ended with a scramble to avoid relegation and a lost Coupe de France final
clubs.notes: Returning loanees form the core of an early rebuild under Pantaloni; no major permanent fees confirmed yet for this snapshot.

clubs.name: Stade Rennais
clubs.managerNote: No change — in post since February 2026
clubs.notes: Rennes back Haise with six additions, led by Mayenda at ~€22m.

clubs.name: RC Lens
clubs.managerNote: New — German coach, signed through 2028, replacing Pierre Sage, who left for Crystal Palace; Lens are now on their third straight summer with a new head coach
clubs.notes: Sangaré's ~€48m sale to Brentford is the standout outgoing, funding Cuisance's arrival.

clubs.name: RC Strasbourg
clubs.managerNote: New — Portuguese coach, replacing Gary O'Neil, who left for Ipswich Town
clubs.notes: Emegha's ~€25.3m move to Chelsea funds Sousa's arrival.

clubs.name: Toulouse FC
clubs.managerNote: New — Danish coach, replaced Carles Martínez Novell, who left for Bayer Leverkusen
clubs.notes: No major confirmed transfers found yet for this snapshot.

clubs.name: Stade Brestois
clubs.managerNote: New — promoted into the role after the death of Éric Roy, the club's longtime manager, on 17 June 2026 at age 58 following a battle with pancreatic cancer
clubs.notes: Lachuer steps up after the tragic passing of Éric Roy, with Nonge the first arrival.

clubs.name: Le Havre AC
clubs.managerNote: No change — extended his contract by one year plus an option, since July 2024
clubs.notes: No major confirmed transfers found yet for this snapshot.

clubs.name: Angers SCO
clubs.managerNote: New — arrived from Paris FC, replacing Alexandre Dujeux, who moved the other way to Lorient
clubs.notes: Abdelli's departure to Marseille is the only confirmed move so far.

clubs.name: AJ Auxerre
clubs.managerNote: New — Belgian-English coach, replaced Christophe Pélissier
clubs.notes: Sinayoko's move to PSG is the window's headline departure.

clubs.name: Paris FC
clubs.managerNote: New — replaced Antoine Kombouaré
clubs.notes: Rosenior's first window is aggressive: three arrivals totalling ~€57.5m.

clubs.name: FC Lorient
clubs.managerNote: New — arrived from Angers, replacing Olivier Pantaloni, who left for Nice
clubs.notes: No major confirmed transfers found yet for this snapshot; club sources describe an intersession built on continuity rather than upheaval.

clubs.name: ESTAC Troyes
clubs.managerNote: No change — led Troyes to the 2025/26 Ligue 2 title

playersIn.detail: Australian goalkeeper, part of the City Football Group network, ~€1.7m

playersOut.detail: ~€25m, City Football Group deal; expected to be loaned to Monaco

rumours: Sankhoun Diawara — linked with Rangers, unconfirmed
clubs.notes: Promoted Troyes bank ~€25m for Detourbet while adding Beach from the City Football Group network.

clubs.name: Le Mans FC
clubs.managerNote: No change — led the club to back-to-back promotions
clubs.notes: Back-to-back promotions bring measured additions. The club was recently taken over by Brazilian investment fund Outfield; former Lyon/PSG sporting director Bruno Cheyrou has joined as a football adviser.
